findings.finding: Three peers reported after Centene last spoke (07-28), and all three read positively on the lines Centene trades on. Elevance (10-21) raised 2026 guidance, said its Medicaid operating margin will land slightly ahead of its -1.75% forecast on stronger-than-expected July 1 state rate updates, and said ACA claims 'continue to develop favorably'. Molina (10-21) printed a 93.0% Medicaid MCR on 'rate updates and stable medical cost trend', a Marketplace MCR 'in line with normal seasonality', and called 'the beginning of the turn in Medicaid margins' on 2027 rates. UnitedHealth (10-13) beat and raised. Centene guided Q2 and Q3 Medicaid HBR above Q1 (93.1%) and the full year at about 93.5% (Q2 was 93.9%), so a Q3 Medicaid HBR at or below about 93.9% plus 2027 rate commentary like its peers' would sit at the good end of what was guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peer reactions to these same signals were mixed. MOH fell about 8.5% intraday on 10-21 despite a beat and a reaffirmed guide (goldesel.de, 2026-10-21); UNH gained about 3% (XTB, 2026-10-13). Centene's own Medicaid-HBR beats: Q1 2026 +13.95%, Q2 2026 -0.27%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: CNC is up 8.7% over 20 days, which spans the UNH and ELV prints. If the Medicaid read-through were fully in the price, the skew would not be +5 vol points to the downside, and the stock would have run through its 52-week high rather than sitting 4.6% below it. MOH's sell-off on similar Medicaid numbers shows the market is not paying peers for this line yet.
findings.independence: Molina 8-K 10-21 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001179929/000117992926000042/moh3q26_er.htm) and UNH 10-13 (https://www.xtb.com/en/market-analysis/unitedhealth-group-shares-gain-3-after-stronger-than-expected-earnings-and-guidance) are separate documents pointing the same way. This is peer read-through (a proxy), not a Centene number.

findings.finding: The Q3 bar is set unusually low by Centene itself ('a little above breakeven'; consensus about $0.07-0.09), and in 2026 the company has run well ahead of its own expectations. Q1 adjusted EPS of $3.37 was 'about $0.50 above the company's expectations'; Q2 was $2.51 against about $1.02 consensus (about $0.50 of it was non-recurring 2025 settlements). The FY floor went from >$3.40 to >$4.80 in one quarter. H1 adjusted EPS is $5.88, so the >$4.80 floor implies an H2 loss of about $1.08, against consensus about -$0.99. Any Q3 print above about $0.10 lifts the FY floor mechanically, unless Q4 is guided down.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a $1.49 EPS beat and floor raised from >$3.40 to >$4.80, stock -0.27%. Q1 2026: a $0.50 beat and raise, +13.95%. Q3 2025: +12.5%. Beat-and-raise has paid on 2 of the last 3 prints, and the largest beat bought nothing.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus is still at about $0.08 and FY $4.89, only about $0.09 above the floor. If the street expected a repeat of Q1/Q2's beat pattern, FY consensus would sit well above the floor, as it did not after Q2. Still, a beat on a near-zero bar is widely anticipated in managed care, and Q2 showed the stock will not pay for a beat that is mostly non-recurring.
findings.independence: Q1 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001071739/000107173926000099/a20260428ex991pressrelease.htm) and Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001071739/000107173926000154/a20260728ex991pressrelease.htm). Both are the company's own documents, so this is not independent of the company. It shares a date with finding 1 but rests on separate evidence.

findings.finding: Management said it will give 'a better viewpoint' on 2027 on this Q3 call. The bridge is hard on Centene's own words. About $0.50 of 2026 EPS is 2025 settlements that 'would not recur in 2027'. OB3 Medicaid expansion attrition is 'mid-single digit' over 2027-2029. Rate lag 'mutes' margin recovery through H2 2026 and part of 2027, with acceleration only 'late 2027'. Centene is exiting New Hampshire ACA and Arkansas ARHOME (about 77k members). FY2027 consensus is $5.34 (range $4.99-6.25) against an FY2026 consensus of $4.89; ex the $0.50 non-recurring that base is about $4.39, so the street needs about 22% underlying growth. An early 2027 framing below about $5 is a guidance miss on the line this stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First-look outlooks have moved this name the most: 2025-07-01 guidance withdrawal -40.37%, and Q4 2025 (02-05, 2026 guide) -3.66%. Q3 2025 commentary (10-28-2025) +12.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the +5 vol-point put skew and a 7.7% implied move are consistent with this risk. It would be fully priced if FY27 consensus already sat below $5 or if the stock had sold off after MOH. Instead consensus is $5.34 and the stock is near its high. A possible offset: if roughly $0.96 of 2026 severance and optimization cost sits inside adjusted EPS (the Q2 release says 2026 estimates 'include' about $0.76 severance and $0.20 optimization; whether that is adjusted or GAAP is unclear), it would add back and roughly close the gap.
findings.independence: Peers pointed the other way on 2027 Medicaid rates (ELV 'encouraged by what we're seeing in our 2027 rates'; MOH 'strength of recent rate updates for 2027'), which is why the range is wide and the size small. FY27 consensus comes from one undated aggregator snippet (https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/cnc), so this is capped small.

findings.finding: CMS said on 2026-09-22 it would cancel about 315,000 Marketplace enrollments covering more than 760,000 people as improper, recoup the associated subsidies, and freeze new agent/broker registration for plan year 2027. Centene is the largest on-exchange carrier (about 3.5M Marketplace members at 06-30), so a share of the cancellations, a subsidy clawback, or a reserve could land in Q3 or the 2026 Marketplace margin (guided 4.5-5%). Oscar flagged 250-300k of its own members in August and said the effect was in its guidance; Centene has disclosed no number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Marketplace was the line behind the 2025-07-01 -40.37% (risk-adjustment shock). Q2 2026's Marketplace favourability came with a flat reaction (-0.27%).
findings.why_not_priced: No Centene-specific figure exists in any source found, and the stock rose after 09-22. If the market had sized a Centene exposure, there would be an analyst cut or a gap down around 09-22/23 and some commentary; none was found. Mechanism and timing (retroactive or not, who repays) are not stated, which keeps the size small. Removing zero-claim enrollees could also help Centene's risk-adjustment position.
findings.independence: Oscar's own disclosure (Becker's, https://www.beckerspayer.com/?p=27520, Aug 2026; 403, read via snippet) confirms carriers book an effect. This is industry-level, not a Centene number.

findings.finding: The 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings released by CMS on 10-08 (they set 2028 quality bonuses) cut Centene's share of members in 4+ star plans from 18% to 9% (Stephens, via Becker's). Centene's unweighted average fell from 3.31 to 3.14, and five Wellcare contracts are at 2.5 stars or below. Capstone called it likely neutral for Centene. The call may quantify the 2028 bonus loss inside a Medicare segment that management targets at 'break even or better' for 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Stars updates have moved CNC before (Bloomberg Government: 'Centene Surges on ... Star Scores Update', https://news.bgov.com/insurance/centene-surges-on-positive-view-of-early-medicare-quality-scores). The stock has looked through this one so far, rising after 10-08.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: public for three weeks and the stock rose through it. Only a dollar figure on the call would be new. Net of the company, Medicare Advantage is about 1M of 25.9M at-risk members and the money arrives in 2028, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Healthcare Finance News list of 2027 ratings (https://www.healthcarefinancenews.com/news/see-list-plans-medicare-advantage-star-ratings-2027). Same CMS data, so this is not independent evidence.

findings.finding: Ambetter announced on 10-20 that it is expanding into 55 more counties for plan year 2027, while keeping about 3.5M members across 27 states. Management had said on 07-28 that it would 'get visibility into our competitive positioning as we get into Q3', so expanding after seeing competitors' filed rates suggests it is comfortable with 2027 Marketplace pricing and margin. This comes on top of large requested increases (Ambetter about +40% average in Pennsylvania).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Marketplace margin restoration drove the Q1 2026 +13.95% (Marketplace HBR 75.3%) and the guide raise to 4.5-5% margin in Q2 (-0.27%).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a product press release that the wires read as marketing, not as a pricing signal. If it were priced as a margin read, 2027 consensus would carry Marketplace growth, and the 2027 debate (finding 3) is about Medicaid attrition instead. It is an inference from the company's own action, not a number.
findings.independence: Pennsylvania rate requests (https://whyy.org/articles/premium-increases-2027-pennie-pennsylvania-aca/) show Ambetter pricing for margin. Fierce Healthcare 'Centene, Oscar Health outline 2027 ACA marketplace plans' (https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/payers/centene-oscar-health-outline-2027-aca-marketplace-plans, 403, not read).

findings.finding: Centene redeemed all of its remaining $568.7M of 4.25% notes due December 2027 on 2026-10-23, from cash and ahead of the print. That clears a 2027 maturity and is consistent with the strong statutory and parent cash that its 2026 raises imply. It is a modest positive or a zero.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction to debt actions found.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and small. What the money buys: the redemption retires debt early rather than raising money, so it signals liquidity, not distress. It matters only if the call ties it to a buyback restart.

outside_window.finding: OB3 Medicaid community-engagement (work) requirements start in 2027, with mid-single-digit expansion attrition over 2027-2029 per management. States committed to revisit rates at 1/1/2027. The membership effect lands after the window; only the guidance framing (finding 3) is inside it.

baseline_tension: The evidence is balanced. Peer read-through and the low Q3 bar lean up, against the +5 put skew. The 2027-bridge risk agrees with the skew and the near-high price, so the net sits close to zero, and p_up is held at 52.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the Q3 beat finding is cut from +0.8 to +0.5, because Q2's $1.49 beat and big raise bought -0.27%.
Lesson 5 / 'What has worked' (a peer's print after the company last spoke): the peer read-through is kept at +1.0 rather than shrunk as a proxy.
Lesson 7: short interest was checked before the negatives (about 3% of float, 2.4-3.3 days, not crowded), so the 2027 negative is not shrunk for squeeze risk; it agrees with the skew.
Lesson 4: the notes redemption was asked what it buys (early repayment from cash) and is signed as a small positive.

Lesson 6: the bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing estimate sources for Q3. FY27 consensus has a single undated source, so the 2027 finding stays capped small. The OB3 effect is moved to outside_window.
